titolo: Why Did the US Get Rich But Latin America Never Did?

cartellino.fonte: GDP per capita, current US$, 2023, World Bank (USA about $82,000; Latin America and Caribbean about $9,000 average, World Bank regional aggregate)

mondi.prompt_en: Ground-level photo at the US-Mexico border in Tijuana and San Diego, at the border fence. Left side: San Diego, tidy suburban streets, new SUVs, manicured lawns, large houses. Right side: Tijuana hillside with crowded colorful self-built homes, dusty unpaved road, old cars. One ordinary man in a casual T-shirt stands exactly on the border line, one foot on each side, looking at the camera with a surprised expression.

titolo: Why Did Russia Unify as a Country But Europe Never Did?

cartellino.fonte: GDP per capita, current US$, 2023, World Bank (EU27 ≈ $44,000 vs Russia ≈ $13,000)

mondi.prompt_en: Ground-level photo at the real Estonia–Russia border in Narva and Ivangorod, split by the Narva River and bridge. Left side Estonia: restored medieval castle, tidy cafés, modern cars, bright shop windows. Right side Russia: Ivangorod's aging concrete apartment blocks, faded facades, cracked pavement. One ordinary man stands exactly on the border line, one foot on each side, looking at the camera, surprised.

titolo: Why Britain's Decline Is Making Ireland Rich

cartellino.fonte: GDP per capita, current US$, 2022-2023 (approx.), World Bank. Ireland ~$100,000-105,000 vs UK ~$49,000-52,000. Note: Irish GDP is inflated by multinational profit shifting.

mondi.prompt_en: Photorealistic ground-level view of the Irish border near Strabane and Lifford, a road crossing with a small bridge over the River Foyle. Left side: Ireland, modern glass office buildings of tech firms, new cars, tidy streets, bright signage. Right side: Northern Ireland (UK), older worn terraced houses, boarded-up shops, cracked pavement, grey drizzle. A single ordinary man in a casual jacket stands exactly on the white border line, one foot on each side, looking at the camera with a surprised expression.

titolo: Switzerland Should Be Poor. Here's Why It Isn't

cartellino.fonte: GDP per capita, current US$, 2023, World Bank (Switzerland ~$93,000; Italy ~$38,000; Austria, Germany and France are all poorer than Switzerland)

mondi.prompt_en: Photorealistic ground-level view at the Swiss-Italian border at Chiasso-Como. Left side Switzerland: spotless clean street, modern glass bank buildings, new Mercedes and Teslas, flower boxes on windows. Right side Italy: older faded apartment buildings, peeling plaster, cracked pavement, small scooters, shuttered shops. One ordinary man in a casual jacket stands exactly on the painted border line, one foot on each side, looking at the camera with a surprised expression.

titolo: The Extreme Geography Behind The World's Richest Countries

mondi.prompt_en: Ground-level photo at the real border between Spain and Morocco at Ceuta: left side Spain, clean modern street, glass buildings, new cars, tidy sidewalks; right side Morocco, dusty road, crowded improvised stalls, worn concrete houses.
